data.summary: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py _private_addresses passes ipaddress a zero-padded octet (172.16.001.1, 010.0.0.1), which raises ValueError and is silently skipped, so a private address written that way is committed without the guard failing; found by the B-upstream-redact critic. chunk_findings.detail: The home-path substitution is skipped whenever the resolved home directory is `/root`, and nothing else in the pass covers `/root`: `_HOME_PATH` only matches `/(?:home|Users)/...` and `_TILDE_PATH` only matches `~/...`. So with `redact_report("credentials at /root/.aws/credentials and /root/.ssh/id_rsa", home="/root")` the returned text is unchanged — the paths survive, contradicting the module's stated property that home paths are removed. The same happens in the environment the docstring describes as the default, because `home=None` resolves through `os.path.expanduser("~")`, which is `/root` for uid 0; running the report generator as root (standard in CI containers) therefore leaks every `/root/...` path such as `/root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/root/.aws/credentials`, `/root/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, which is exactly what this pass is supposed to prevent. Excluding `/root` may have been intended to avoid redacting web-path fragments like `example.com/root`, but that also removes the only protection for the root user's home, and the acceptance criterion ("no /home/<user> ... remains") is silently not met for the root user.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/redact_report.py` — `redact_report`, the `home_dir not in ("/", "~", "/root")` guard

chunk_findings.detail: The corpus test derives its entire fixture from `ROOT / ".ddflow" / "events"` and then hard-asserts on properties of that directory: `assert len(bugs) > 50` and `assert projects`. The docstring/decision text says `.ddflow/events` is *not committed* (it is only exempted from the repo-is-generic scan). On any clean checkout — CI, a fresh clone, another developer's machine, or a run via an installed wheel — `_events()` returns `[]`, so `_bugs()` is `[]` and the test dies at `assert len(bugs) > 50` (and if the count assertion were relaxed, `_corpus_hostname()` crashes one line earlier with `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` at `return max(counts, key=counts.__getitem__)`, and `_corpus_projects` would make `assert projects` fail because the glob-based regex finds nothing). Concretely: `rm -rf .ddflow/events && pytest tests/test_redact_report.py::test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean` fails, i.e. the test only passes on the author's machine that happens to hold ≥50 committed-local `bug.found` events with `.../src|git|code|work|projects/<name>` paths. An acceptance test whose corpus is untracked state cannot gate the change; it needs to skip (or generate the events) when `.ddflow/events` is absent, rather than assert its size.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean / ::\_corpus_hostname

chunk_findings.detail: The home directory is skipped whenever it resolves to `/root`, and the only other home-path detector, `_HOME_PATH`, matches just `/(home|Users)/<user>`. As a result `/root/...` paths are never redacted. This is environment-dependent: running as root (HOME=/root — the norm in Docker/container CI and `docker exec`) makes `os.path.expanduser("~")`/`Path.home()` return `/root`, which the guard rejects, so the home-dir substitution is never applied; `_HOME_PATH` (`/(?:home|Users)/`) and `_TILDE_PATH` (`~/`) do not match either. Concretely, `redact_report("/root/.aws/credentials", home="/root")` returns `"/root/.aws/credentials"` unchanged with empty counts, so a home path (and the sensitive filename under it) leaves the machine. The same happens for a non-root caller whenever the report body references any `/root/...` path. That contradicts the change's stated goal (3) that home paths are removed, and it is exactly the "environment that makes it wrong".

chunk_findings.detail: The test embeds the raw literal `010.0.0.1` and asserts the redactor must count it as an IPv4 redaction (`out.counts["ipv4"] == 2`). Under the leading-zero normalisation that makes that count true (parsing `010` as `10`), `010.0.0.1` is exactly the private 10.x address the whole change is meant to keep out of a committed artifact. The same test file asserts `rr.private_addresses` is identical to `tests/test_repo_is_generic._private_addresses`, and the synthetic fixture elsewhere is built from `_ip(...)`/string pieces explicitly to avoid that scanner. If the shared detector sees `010.0.0.1` as private, the repo-is-generic scan will flag this committed file and fail; if it does not see it that way, the redactor built on that detector cannot produce `ipv4 == 2` and the assertion fails. Either way this literal is inconsistent with the change's own “fabricated addresses built from string pieces” invariant.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::test_zero_padded_and_dot_local_leaks_are_caught

chunk_findings.detail: The helper only discovers project names through paths matching `/home/[\w.-]+/(?:src|git|code|work|projects)/([\w.-]+)`, then `test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean` asserts `projects` is non-empty. Any event log whose paths are recorded as `/Users/<user>/...` (macOS), `<drive>:\Users\...`, or `/home/<user>/<anything-other-than-those-five-subdirs>` yields an empty set and the test fails with "the log should name some other project", even though the leak checker `_leaks` itself accepts `/(?:home|Users)/...` and the intent is generic “home/repo paths”. This makes the suite fail purely on the developer/CI machine’s home layout rather than on a redaction defect.

chunk_findings.detail: The primary acceptance test calls `pytest.skip("no bug.found events in this checkout's log")` whenever `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` contains no `bug.found` events. The file itself documents that `.ddflow/events` is uncommitted, so a fresh CI checkout has no corpus and the test skips. In that environment the only test that runs redaction over the project's real summaries and rendered bundle never executes, so a leak in real bug summaries goes undetected while the suite reports green. Concrete: clone the repo without `.ddflow/events`, run pytest; this test is skipped and the acceptance criterion “generated at test time from .ddflow/events/*.jsonl … no leak remains” is not verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::test_every_bug_summary_and_rendering_is_clean

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "/ddflow/x.py" in out.text, "the repo-relative tail is kept"` requires the redactor to preserve the relative tail of a redacted repo path. The stated intent only requires that no home/repo path remains; it does not require keeping the relative tail or any path structure. A correct implementation that replaces the entire private path `…/work/mysecretrepo/ddflow/x.py` with `[REDACTED:path]` leaves no private data but fails this assertion. The test therefore over-constrains the output format and can reject a valid redaction implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::test_actual_home_repo_root_and_machine_hostname

chunk_findings.detail: `_corpus_projects` filters out every project name shorter than four characters: `{n for n in names if len(n) >= 4 …}`. The acceptance requires no project name from the runtime-derived list to remain, with no length restriction. Given a log path `/home/u/src/abc/x.py`, the project `abc` is excluded from `projects`, so `_leaks` never checks for `abc` and the redactor is never given `abc` in its `names` argument. A bug summary containing `abc` would pass the test even if the redactor leaks it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::_corpus_projects

chunk_findings.detail: The intent names `[upstream].redact_extra` as a source of extra redaction items, but the suite only exercises `cfg.session.redact_extra`. No test sets or verifies `cfg.upstream.redact_extra`; an implementation that ignores the upstream extra entirely still passes every test in this file. Concrete: `cfg.upstream.redact_extra = ["zzproj"]` with a report containing `zzproj` would leak without any test failing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_report.py::test_configured_secret_patterns_are_applied

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `time.monotonic() - t0 < 5` for a 200,000-character input. This is a wall-clock threshold, not a complexity bound, so it is environment-dependent. On a loaded or slow CI runner the same linear-time implementation can exceed five seconds and fail the test. Concrete: run the test on a CI worker under heavy load; the assertion fails despite the redactor scaling linearly.
